newsitem.title: USA: FORECAST - U.S. Q3 ECI expected around unchanged.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - U.S. Q3 ECI expected around unchanged.

text.p: Economists expect the Employment Cost Index (ECI) to show that the increase in U.S. labor costs in the third quarter was moderate and will not trigger a pickup in inflation that could prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy.

According to a Reuters poll, economists expect the ECI to have increased by 0.8 percent in the third quarter, the same rate of increase as in the previous two quarters. Experts say the index is the most accurate measure of labor costs, which includes salaries and benefits.

"If it stays where it has been, it will be a non-event for the (U.S. Treasury) market," said Carol Stone, senior economist at Nomura Securities International Inc, who predicted a 0.8-percent increase.
The Labor Department will release third-quarter ECI on Tuesday, October 29 at 0830 EST/1330 GMT.

James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc, who also expected the index to increase by 0.8 percent, said market reaction to the number will be subdued. "Trends in wages are changing slowly, so it's harder for the market to get excited. This trend is not threatening for inflation yet."

While bond players may react with a collective yawn if the figure is unchanged, Glassman said the Federal Reserve and Wall Street economists will pay close attention to the wage component of the index, which is an indicator of tightness in the labor market.
Glassman noted that growth in wages has outpaced increases in the cost of employee benefits over the past several quarters, even though the overall ECI has remained the same.
He expected the trend to continue, adding, "What we are seeing is the very first signs that the labor markets are indeed tight. It's not an issue for inflation yet, but it's the beginning."

John Ryding, senior economist at Bear, Stearns and Co Inc, said that while the Federal Reserve will watch the wage component in particular, it is unlikely to sway the central bank's view on interest rates if the overall number remains at current levels.

"The Fed has shown it is not willing to move on an increase in labor cost pressures alone this year. It is waiting to see an overall increase in the (Consumer Price Index) and the (Producer Price Index), and so far we haven't seen either," he said.
